# kimage

> kimage declares immutable, versioned container images as Kubernetes resources,
> manages their production and verified publication to a retained cluster-local
> registry, and resolves workload image selectors to digest-pinned pulls. Apache
> 2.0. Alpha. Public Cargo packages: kimage-core and kimage-control, version 0.5.0.

**When to use it.** Use kimage when inputs are already provisioned in Kubernetes,
when images should remain available independently of source/build cache, or when
a cluster needs local build and pull workflows without an external registry.
Application authors declare an Image, exact version, and source; the controller
handles attempts and publication. There is no per-image BuildRun or output
registry configuration. The registry and node-local serving are included in the
installation; administrators provision storage and installation generates service credentials. Workloads
request Image identity and accepted versions, e.g. platform://apps/service:^1.2.0,
without knowing a registry hostname, repository path, or digest. Admission pins
new Pods; existing Pods do not roll automatically. kpack also declares Images
and exposes registry digest output; declarative Images and ARM64 alone are not
differentiators. kimage combines a retained version catalog, builder, included
registry, and placement-aware workload resolution. See the
[kpack comparison](https://kimage.dev/docs/#kpack).
Shipwright provides configurable build strategies; Tekton handles general task
pipelines. The current kimage builder is narrower than those general workflows.

**Current boundaries.** Builds support Containerfile, strategy Direct,
builderRef default, FROM scratch, provisioned local files, and network-none RUN.
No remote base images, remote ADD/context URLs, external syntax frontends, remote
cache, general base provisioning, signing/attestations,
HA, arbitrary storage/schema migration, or automatic retained-artifact GC.
Administrator-managed builder isolation is not a hostile tenant security claim.

**Install (0.5.0).** Rust 1.99.0+, administrator kubeconfig, Ready Linux
amd64/arm64 nodes, persistent storage and the supported Pod user-namespace runtime:

```sh
cargo install kimage-control --version 0.5.0 --locked --bin kimage --bin kimage-install
kimage install --application-namespace apps
```

No flags means current kubeconfig application namespace, kimage-system system
namespace, installation kimage, 1Gi retained PVC, default StorageClass, port 17701.
The CLI fetches only the exact release's small SHA-verified component-images.json;
kubelet pulls complete digest-pinned native OCI indexes from
 ghcr.io/inferal-oss/kimage (admission,builder,exporter,gateway,input,operator,proxy,registry).
No binary/image uploads through ConfigMaps, installer Pods or port-forwarding.
No required carrier, issuer scripts or source checkout. Registry/admission/builder
credentials are generated in process, with separate CAs and read/publish identities;
CA private keys are not deployed. Reapply identical arguments to resume, preserving
Secrets and administrator build policy. kimage-install is a compatible alias.
The Cargo crate named kimage is unrelated. Prebuilt installers: GitHub releases.
Gateway/proxy serving version remains 0.3.0 separately from Cargo 0.5.0.

**Helm alternative.** Helm 3.14+ with live cluster access:

```sh
helm repo add kimage https://kimage.dev/charts
helm repo update
kubectl create namespace apps
helm install kimage kimage/kimage --version 0.5.0 \
  --namespace kimage-system --create-namespace \
  --set applicationNamespace=apps --wait --wait-for-jobs
```

Published charts contain the same eight native index pins. Helm discovers live
Nodes; offline template requires full Node objects via nodes. It does not create
the application namespace. Values: scope namespace|cluster; applicationNamespace
(default default for namespace scope); excludedNamespaces list; runtimeProfile
inferal|k3s; persistence.storageClass/size(default1Gi)/existingClaim; registryNode;
port(default17701); workerNodes arch-to-node map; buildPolicy(empty preserves
existing or defaults OnDemand, can Eager); images.repository and images.digests.
The operator manages shared CRDs; Helm does not own/delete them.

**Runtime prerequisites.** Default inferal profile: RKE2 v1.36.5+rke2r1 /
containerd 2.3.4-k3s1. Tested k3s profile: K3s v1.36.5+k3s1 / containerd
2.3.4-k3s1.36; add --runtime-profile k3s or Helm --set runtimeProfile=k3s.
Untested exact versions are refused. Generic kind/k3d is not automatically
supported. User namespaces, idmapped volumes, kernel/filesystem support, CNI
policies and storage matter. BuildKit 0.33.0 / builtin frontend1.27.0 workers use
hostUsers:false, native snapshotter, no host/runtime mounts or SA token, bounded
nested namespace capabilities and unconfined seccomp/AppArmor inside their Pod.
This is administrator-managed isolation, not a hostile-tenant guarantee.

**Delivery and mirrors.** GHCR supplies system components. The included retained
cluster-local registry stores application images, whose publication needs no
external registry configuration. Nodes need HTTPS access to GHCR or an approved
mirror. Mirror all eight complete multi-platform indexes preserving digests;
change only repository in an independently verified local catalog and pass
--image-catalog /path/component-images.json. Helm: set images.repository and
retain published digest pins. Nodes must already trust/reach the mirror; kimage
does not alter trust stores or import images through the API. Catalog alone is
not enough for disconnected use. Optional KIMAGE_GITHUB_TOKEN applies only to
fixed GitHub metadata requests, never asset downloads. Catalog size/asset SHA,
roles, versions, API revision and both native platforms are checked.

**Minimal complete build example.** Assumes namespace apps and default builder
are already configured. On native Linux/amd64 or Linux/arm64 with Rust and a musl linker, create a small
program in hello.rs: `fn main() { println!("Hello from kimage!"); loop {
std::thread::park_timeout(std::time::Duration::from_secs(3600)); } }`.

```sh
case "$(uname -m)" in
  x86_64) ARCH=amd64; TARGET=x86_64-unknown-linux-musl ;;
  aarch64) ARCH=arm64; TARGET=aarch64-unknown-linux-musl ;;
  *) echo "Use a supported Linux build machine"; exit 1 ;;
esac
rustup target add "$TARGET"
mkdir -p .local/tutorial
rustc --edition=2024 --target "$TARGET" \
  -C opt-level=z -C strip=symbols -C panic=abort hello.rs -o ".local/tutorial/hello-$ARCH"
# On a mixed cluster, collect both architecture binaries here before this step.
kubectl -n apps create configmap hello-context --from-file=.local/tutorial \
  --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
```

On macOS use a matching native Linux machine or build container for that executable; a
native macOS binary cannot run inside the scratch image. Save as image.yaml:

```yaml
apiVersion: kimage.dev/v1alpha1
kind: Image
metadata:
  name: hello
  namespace: apps
spec:
  version: "1.0.0"
  source:
    build:
      format: Containerfile
      execution: {strategy: Direct, builderRef: default}
      cache: {mode: Local}
      definition:
        inline: |
          FROM scratch
          ARG TARGETARCH
          COPY hello-${TARGETARCH} /hello
          ENTRYPOINT ["/hello"]
      inputs:
        contextPath: /workspace/context
        volumes:
          - name: context
            configMap:
              name: hello-context
              defaultMode: 365
        volumeMounts:
          - {name: context, mountPath: /workspace/context, readOnly: true}
```

Mode 365 is decimal for octal 0555. Apply the Image and Deployment, wait for verified publication, and run
the downloadable Deployment (or use the selector in your own Pod template):

```sh
kubectl apply -f image.yaml
# Automatic Images remain AwaitingDemand until a workload requests them.
kubectl apply -f https://kimage.dev/examples/hello/deployment.yaml
kubectl -n apps wait --for=condition=Ready image/hello --timeout=10m
kubectl -n apps get imagereleases
kubectl -n apps rollout status deployment/hello --timeout=5m
kubectl -n apps logs deployment/hello
```

The workload's image field is quoted YAML:

```yaml
containers:
  - name: hello
    image: "platform://apps/hello:^1.0.0"
    imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
```

Admission leaves workload templates symbolic and pins actual CREATE Pods,
including init containers, to
127.0.0.1:<port>/<namespace>/<image-uid>@sha256:<digest>, with IfNotPresent and
eligible-node constraints. Kubelet uses its normal runtime and node-local proxy.
Changing a range/channel affects newly created Pods, not existing Pods; use exact
versions for a uniform rollout. Unsupported image-update/ephemeral-container
paths are rejected. Create replacements through the workload controller.

**Workload compatibility.** Deployments, StatefulSets, DaemonSets, ReplicaSets,
ReplicationControllers, and Jobs use spec.template.spec.containers[].image (or
initContainers[].image). CronJobs use
spec.jobTemplate.spec.template.spec.containers[].image (or initContainers).
Regular containers, init containers, and native restartPolicy: Always init
sidecars all resolve through actual Pod CREATE admission. Custom controllers work
when their schema/validation accepts platform:// and they copy the selector
unchanged into a Pod image field in the configured application namespace. The
controller may run elsewhere; the Image and Pod must share the application scope.
Controllers that pre-parse OCI references, fetch image metadata before creating
Pods, or rewrite selectors require integration. No arbitrary CRD field scanning
is performed. Image strings in ConfigMaps, env/args, Containerfiles, image-backed
volumes, static Pods, or ephemeral-container updates are not supported selectors
in 0.3.0. Edit workload templates for ordinary rollouts; publishing versions or
moving channels does not itself restart workloads. Full reference:
https://kimage.dev/docs/#workload-compatibility

**Platforms and build policy (0.3.0).** Omitted spec.platform/spec.platforms means
native automatic selection. Default policy is OnDemand: without a consumer,
automatic Images remain AwaitingDemand and no worker build starts. Administrator
ConfigMap <installation>-config in the system namespace has data.configuration.json
set to {"schema":1,"buildPolicy":"OnDemand"}; change buildPolicy to "Eager" to build
all available supported platforms before consumers exist. The operator watches
changes; installation preserves this config.

Admission evaluates actual Pod nodeName, nodeSelector and required nodeAffinity
against eligible Ready nodes with approved local proxies. Only amd64 placement
builds/uses amd64; only arm64 placement builds/uses arm64. If both remain possible,
build both and pin a fully verified OCI index, whose native child kubelet selects.
One eligible architecture needs one variant. Preferred affinity does not narrow
the platform set. All managed containers' platform constraints are intersected.
Unsupported/contradictory placement fails; there is no automatic build emulation.
Admission preserves required placement and restricts scheduling to verified native
platforms and eligible nodes.

Explicit spec.platform: {os: linux, architecture: arm64} requests one native build.
Alternatively use spec.platforms as a list of native platform objects, omitting
platform, to explicitly request a set. These are direct build requests, even under
OnDemand. Available native architectures bound builds. Version identity is Image
UID + version + platform; the aggregate index has its own immutable key. Native
refs appear in status.platformReleases; status.releaseRef points at the available
native or aggregate release. Adding arm64 cannot overwrite published amd64 bytes.
Aggregates require matching private ordinary/definition captures and object/PVC
identities across variants; changed sources require a new version.

A real unresolved Pod CREATE records bounded ImageDemand for the current Image
UID/generation/version and requested platforms, then fails with ImageBuildPending.
Workload controllers retry while the operator produces the image. Direct Pod apply
may need a retry after Image Ready. Server dry-run records no demand. Do not wait
for an automatic Image before applying its Deployment. Demand accumulates within
a generation; stale UIDs/generations and arbitrary historical build requests fail.

The CLI and Helm discover one native worker per available architecture and a
read proxy per eligible node. Component indexes select native manifests through
kubelet, independent of laptop architecture. From 0.5.0, eligible nodes and
platforms reconcile automatically under node policy; earlier releases require
reapplication after node additions. The original registry node/UID stays pinned
to protect retained storage; replacement
needs explicit recovery. There is no QEMU emulation.

Copied executable inputs must match the requested architecture. The hello example
uses ARG TARGETARCH and COPY hello-${TARGETARCH}; provide hello-amd64 and hello-arm64
for a mixed cluster. A homogeneous cluster needs only its matching binary. kimage
does not translate source binaries. Compile these on matching native Linux build
machines, then populate the input ConfigMap directory before applying workloads.

**Installation scope.** Default --scope namespace targets the current kubeconfig
namespace, or explicit --application-namespace apps. --scope cluster omits application-namespace, manages
ordinary namespaces including future ones, and accepts repeated --exclude-namespace
NAME flags. The system namespace and kube-system/kube-public/kube-node-lease are
always excluded from application admission/reconciliation. Overlaps with other
kimage installations are refused; scope is checkpoint-bound and not changed by a
rerun. Both scopes require cluster administrator setup for shared CRDs/webhooks.
Namespace mode uses application Roles; cluster mode has broader application RBAC
plus runtime scope filters. Images, inputs, destination credentials and selectors
stay in the consuming namespace: platform://other-ns/image is denied even in cluster
mode. Each namespace may define its own same-named Image. Optional exporter follows
this scope. Namespace routing is not hostile-tenant registry confidentiality.

Native Kubernetes E2E tests both installation scopes on amd64 and arm64, real
builds/pulls and built-in/custom controllers, default/on-demand/eager policy,
dry-run, RBAC and namespace boundaries, exclusions and retained PVC on uninstall.
The release workflow requires the matrix to pass before crates/GitHub publication.

**Selector rules.** `platform://apps/hello:1.2.4` selects that exact release;
`:^1.2.0` selects the highest compatible published release below 2.0.0;
`:~1.2.0` stays in the 1.2 patch series; `:stable` reads the explicit mapping
`spec.channels: {stable: "1.2.4"}`. A channel does not produce that version.
Colon ranges start with ^, ~, >, <, =, or *. Compound ranges such as
`platform://apps/hello:>=1.2.0, <2.0.0` work in quoted YAML. Numeric-leading
colon selectors must be complete exact versions: :1.2 and :1.2.* are rejected.
The readable query `platform://apps/hello?version=^1.2.0` and the older encoded
query `?version=%5E1.2.0` both work, decoded once. Colon selectors use literal
characters. Do not combine a colon selector with a query. Prereleases need an
explicitly matching prerelease requirement. No implicit latest, version build
metadata, or cross-namespace consumption. The application webhook is fail-closed;
its outage can block other Pod creation in scope too. Direct internal registry
references and opt-in label bypasses are not supported consumption paths.

**Image and input contracts.** Image/ImageRelease use kimage.dev/v1alpha1.
Choose exactly one source.build or source.ociArchive. An Image UID/version is
immutable after publication; differing output is VersionConflict, so request a
new exact version. Image recreation gets a new UID/repository. Published releases
survive source/Image/cache removal. ConfigMap/Secret inputs freeze UID and
resourceVersion per attempt. Mounted definitions use definition.fromFile.path;
ordinary definitions live under /workspace/inputs, secret definitions under
/run/kimage-build-secrets, independently of COPY contextPath. Mounts must be
read-only and non-overlapping. Traversal and symlink escapes are rejected.
PVC inputs need inputs.producerHandoff:true and stopped producers; this is not
an atomic filesystem snapshot. Use buildSecrets to bind declared Secret files
to RUN --mount=type=secret; keep them outside ordinary context. Secret values do
not automatically invalidate cache: use a non-sensitive cache.invalidationToken
when needed. Local cache is disposable; Disabled requests a no-cache solve.
Cancellation fences the dedicated worker and clears its cache.

OCI archive sources require a same-namespace claimName, relative path,
producerHandoff:true, and expected root {mediaType,digest,size}. Root digest is
not the archive-file checksum. Files must be readable by UID 65532. Complete
original OCI bytes, platform, compressed layer digests, and DiffIDs are verified.
Native amd64/arm64 manifests, nested indexes and complete multi-platform indexes are supported; zstd, descriptor URLs/embedded data, and subject/referrer graphs are unsupported.
`kimage-install schemas` prints full CRD JSON without changing the cluster.

**Upgrade and rollback (0.5.0).** Install the new CLI separately from cluster changes.
Supported edge: published 0.4.1 <-> 0.5.0 only. Use `kimage upgrade --to 0.5.0 --check`,
then the same without --check. `kimage rollback --to 0.4.1 --check`, then without
--check reverses the compatible edge. Add --namespace/--installation as needed.
Check is read-only. Exact catalogs, an exclusive installation Lease and persisted
phases make the operation resumable. Stop old clients/workers before component
policy replacement. Preserve PVC/PV, credentials, admin policy, scope and CRDs.
No storage/schema migration or implicit latest. After interruption, repeat the
same target/catalog; a crashed Lease expires in 30s. Never delete the journal or
switch targets while pending. Completion requires readiness and retained identity
verification; failure does not silently roll back. New managed admission/builds
and uncached pulls may pause; running containers remain controlled by their workloads.
Helm-managed installs require Helm 3 or 4 on PATH. Helm 4 transitions select ordinary three-way updates to avoid
field-ownership conflicts with quiescing and reconciled node resources. They use
exact target pins, retaining ownership/history; rollback renders the exact older chart against current placement as a new
Helm revision. New charts reject unguarded cross-release upgrade.
Old charts cannot add guards to raw helm rollback; use the guarded CLI path.
Helm recovery history must match live credential and build-policy bytes. On
HelmRecoveryCredentialDrift/HelmRecoveryPolicyDrift, reapply the current version's
chart to record the live values, then repeat preflight. Never bypass this check.
`kimage install` only resumes the same release. No bootstrap 0.3.x adoption.
`kimage status --json` shows versions, operation phase, native workers and storage.
`kimage doctor --json` also checks resource drift and current/30-day certificate
validity; unhealthy exits nonzero. Both are read-only and omit credential values.

The release-compatibility.json asset documents exact tested edges and persisted
formats. Unknown/skipped edges are refused. Before returning to 0.4.1, restore
nodePolicy.nodeSelector={} because that operator cannot enforce node selection.
Pins and build policy are preserved. Never replay historical departed-node
placement to recover a pending revision.

**Nodes.** Operator reconciles eligible membership automatically, adds UID-bound
proxies/native workers, and revokes stale approvals. Automatic workers stay put
while eligible. Replacement acquires a worker Lease, terminates old clients and
waits for deletion before replacement; fencing can remain pending for an
unreachable worker. Never force-delete it to bypass safety. Registry node name,
UID and PVC never move automatically. Optional ConfigMap INSTALL-node-policy,
label kimage.dev/installation=INSTALL, data policy.json:
{"schema":1,"nodeSelector":{"kimage.dev/pool":"images"},"workerPins":{"arm64":"arm-worker"}}
Empty selector includes all eligible nodes. Registry must stay selected. Pins
must exist; missing pins report an issue. Helm nodePolicy=null preserves edits;
first-install workerNodes values become pins. System components restart through
ordinary external pulls independently of the included registry.
NodeReconcileForbidden means check the operator's system namespace Role and
RoleBinding against the exact release manifests. Pod/Job metadata patch access
belongs only to that system namespace, not application namespaces or admission.

kimage uninstall --namespace kimage-system --installation kimage, or helm uninstall
kimage --namespace kimage-system --wait, preserves PVCs, CRDs, Images and releases.
After rollback to 0.4.1, first scale deployment/INSTALLATION-operator to zero and
wait for its operator Pods to be deleted, delete its named INSTALLATION-builder-amd64
and INSTALLATION-builder-arm64 Pods with --ignore-not-found --wait=true, then helm
uninstall. Published 0.4.1 recreates workers without Helm tracking metadata.
Use the installation label plus kimage.dev/role=operator for the Pod wait.
CLI uninstall already stops supervisors first. Fresh 0.5.0 Helm removal is
tested directly; predecessor removal uses the documented shutdown procedure.
Never remove retained namespaces/backends/finalizers as normal cleanup. Back up
whole registry backend plus release UIDs, roots and schema coordination state.
No automatic retained-artifact GC or purge. Generated leaves last ten years;
reapply preserves them and does not perform automatic renewal/CA rotation.
Version 0.4.1 fixes intermittent CLI uninstall CleanupIdentityConflict during Pod
status races while retaining UID/spec/ownership guards. For an existing 0.4.0
installation, update the CLI to 0.5.0 and run the same uninstall command. No
component reinstallation or data migration is needed for this cleanup fix.
Published CLI and public Helm mixed-cluster checks cover native GHCR pulls, all
three fresh-Image placement cases, and complete retained OCI graph readback after
uninstall/reinstall: https://github.com/inferal-oss/kimage/blob/main/docs/mixed-install-results.json

**Optional export.** Enable at CLI install with repeated --export-origin
https://registry.example/ flags, or Helm exporter.approvedOrigins list. Empty
disables the separate exporter. Only explicit HTTPS origins are approved. Image spec.exports contains named registry destinations with
repository (authority/path), explicit tags, credentialsSecretRef or explicit
unauthenticated:true, optional caSecretRef with ca.crt, and overwritePolicy:Never.
Credential Secret type is kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson, with auths matching the
exact authority/port. Basic auth or anonymous only; no Bearer exchange/helpers.
Original retained graph bytes are copied and remotely verified without a rebuild.
Existing same-digest tags are idempotent; differing tags are TagConflict. Other
writers require registry-side immutability. Export status/retries are separate
from internal Ready. Target removal/Image deletion never deletes remote content.

**Diagnostics and trust.** Read Image status.conditions/observedGeneration,
operation/releaseRef/build, separate status.exports, and normal Pod events.
Operator/admission expose /metrics on health listeners; proxy 0.3.0 exposes it
on its canonical-authority loopback listener, inspectable by API forwarding.
Stage counters/durations cover build/publication/pull without identity labels.
Check catalog/node sample completeness and timestamps before using gauges.
Admission records bounded ImageDemand objects for real missing-release CREATEs; publishers and readers have distinct credentials.
Eligible node administrators are trusted readers; namespace routing is not
hostile-tenant image confidentiality. Native clients keep TLS verification on.
Rust tests run on macOS/arm64 and native Linux/amd64 and Linux/arm64 musl. Separate two-node
acceptance harnesses cover lifecycle/recovery/binary rollback/export and remain historical evidence; native amd64/arm64 namespace/cluster install E2E is now a release gate; historical live bundles predate the latest selector/CLI metadata.

## Reference

- [Handbook, Markdown](https://kimage.dev/docs/index.md): Full tutorial, installation commands, field reference, operations, troubleshooting, and trust model.
- [Hello Image](https://kimage.dev/examples/hello/image.yaml): Complete build declaration used above.
- [Hello Deployment](https://kimage.dev/examples/hello/deployment.yaml): Complete restricted workload using a readable range.
- [Hello program](https://kimage.dev/examples/hello/main.rs): Static Linux tutorial executable source.

## Optional

- [Source and issues](https://github.com/inferal-oss/kimage): Apache 2.0 repository, engineering contracts, release procedure, acceptance receipts, and contribution workflow.

## Build diagnostics

- `kimage builds IMAGE -n apps`: JSON listing active/retained attempt IDs, version, platform, phase, truncation and Image conditions. Use the parent Image name for multi-platform builds.
- `kimage logs IMAGE -n apps --platform linux/arm64 --follow`; use `--attempt FULL_ID` for a specific retry. Follow never switches attempts.
- Logs are bounded 64 KiB tails, latest five attempts per Image/platform in immutable namespace Secrets. They survive build Pod cleanup and controller restarts, but are lost with their owning Image. Collection after worker/API loss can be unavailable; 0.4.1 attempts have no output.
- Raw progress is separately limited to 16 MiB per solve and 1 MiB per record; exceeding it fails with BuildProgressLimit/BuildProgressLineLimit. BuildKit can clip step output upstream. The retained tail is not a complete log archive.
- Build output can contain printed secrets. Require namespace Secret get/list for retained output and Pod get/list/exec for live output. Do not copy raw logs into public releases, status or issues without review. No arbitrary-output redaction is promised.
- Read Image conditions for stable errors. Transient failures use persisted backoff; permanent failures await changed declarations/inputs. An operator restart does not reset them. VersionConflict means use a new exact version. Solve completion precedes publication and verified release readiness.
- During worker recovery, demand waits for worker Pod and service endpoint readiness before input capture; it does not create an empty interrupted attempt just because the replacement worker is starting.
